status: Recommended room schedule; exact products and measured quantities pending
summary: Blackout where people sleep or watch movies; sheers with a separate privacy layer in social rooms; compact practical shades in working and wet areas. Sheers alone are reserved for glazing verified to have no privacy or blackout requirement.
palette: Warm ivory linen-look sheers, ivory or oatmeal blackout curtain faces, and quiet warm-neutral shades. Concealed or slim dark tracks coordinate with walnut, natural oak and restrained black details. Blackout describes the backing, not a black visible curtain.
renderNote: MW-A02 corrects visible openings against original photographs and the blueprint. Day shows open layers; night demonstrates privacy/blackout closed where visible. Bedroom 2 follows the clarified stair-hall/closet layout; Bedroom 5 reverse view interprets its planned front windows. Rendered operation is not a tested privacy or blackout result.

rules.title: Sheers soften daylight; privacy is separate
rules.text: Keep the airy sheer appearance in living rooms, but include an independently operated, non-see-through privacy shade behind it. An open-weave solar screen is not a substitute for an evening privacy layer. Test the actual sample from outside with the room lights on; silhouettes can remain visible through some light-filtering fabrics.

rules.title: Blackout requires coverage as well as fabric
rules.text: For dual curtains, place sheers closest to the glass and fully closing blackout-lined panels on an independent room-side track. Resolve center overlap, wall returns and top/bottom light gaps. Where furniture prevents functional curtains, substitute a blackout roller behind the sheers. Fabric alone does not guarantee a completely dark room.

rules.title: When just sheers are enough
rules.text: Only where an after-dark sightline check confirms no privacy need and the room has no sleep or cinema requirement. No occupied bedroom or street-facing social room is assigned sheers alone by default. Verified private high glazing can remain bare; a sheer-only treatment there is an aesthetic choice.

rules.title: Keep the construction simple
rules.text: Base pricing assumes manual tracks and cordless shades, retail or semi-custom fabric, and surface-mounted hardware. No rebuilt ceiling pockets or motors. Measure track width, stack-back, opening operation, furniture and floor variation; choose fullness with the fabricator for the actual heading and fabric. Avoid puddled fabric.

rules.title: Price openings once
rules.text: The room amounts below are provisional allowances, not a window count or supplier quotation. Replace them with a labeled opening-by-opening survey before ordering. Interior glazed doors, transoms and terrace doors must be identified separately; windowless rooms receive no new curtain allowance.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · opacity and privacy
sources.note: Sheers offer little privacy; light-filtering fabrics vary in opacity. Manufacturer guidance informs performance distinctions, not the room design or prices.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · blackout and light gaps
sources.note: Mounting, overlaps, liners and side channels influence room darkening. No particular brand or product is specified.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · bathroom window treatments
sources.note: Consider humidity and window location when selecting material; direct shower exposure needs explicit product suitability.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · solar shade limitations
sources.note: A solar-screen shade does not reliably provide nighttime privacy when the interior is illuminated.

rooms.recommendation: No gallery drapes; discreet privacy shade on exterior entrance glass if needed
rooms.coverage: Exterior front-door glazing only, subject to measured fit. Keep internal clear-glass office/media door pairs uncovered in the gallery. High gallery glazing is reviewed separately for neighboring sightlines.
rooms.why: The two-story chandelier, arch and light doors should remain the focus. Full-height curtains add bulk; street-level entrance glass may still need evening privacy.
rooms.day: Entrance shade raised; gallery bright and open.
rooms.night: Lower the entrance privacy shade if the street can see into the house. Keep internal gallery doors visually clear.
rooms.installation: Provisional allowance for one compact door-mounted privacy solution; verify the arched glass, hardware, attachment and door swing. Do not cover inscriptions. Omit the purchase if the actual glass already provides adequate privacy.
rooms.title: Entrance gallery

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + hidden light-filtering privacy shades
rooms.coverage: Both main exterior banks are centered paired 2×2 groups, with TWO structural units in each bank. Preserve the small circular portico-side window and clear internal gallery doors; assess round-window privacy separately on site.
rooms.why: Adjustable glare control helps screen work and calls; a separate privacy layer lets you work after dark without closing the room off all day. Blackout is unnecessary for normal office use.
rooms.day: Sheers soften sun; adjust the shade on the bright side for monitor glare.
rooms.night: Lower privacy shades on both exterior window walls.
rooms.installation: Keep window access, full north-wall cabinetry, southeast desk/chair and door routes clear. Use a non-see-through privacy fabric, not an open solar screen; check it with interior lights on.
rooms.title: Home office

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout-lined curtains; removable clear-door covers for movie mode
rooms.coverage: One REAL centered paired 2×2 street-facing window, plus a separate removable opaque cover for each clear interior door leaf. The sofa wall is SOLID: its smaller exterior window feature is fake, as confirmed by the homeowner, and has no inside opening.
rooms.why: Daylight and gallery light both reduce contrast on the 83-inch TV. Privacy alone is insufficient for the requested theater atmosphere.
rooms.day: Sheers for casual use; close blackout panels for daytime films.
rooms.night: Close blackout panels and fit the room-side door covers for movies; dim lights near the screen.
rooms.installation: Resolve curtain overlap, returns and head gap. Use removable room-side covers with a finish-compatible attachment and storage location; each door must remain operable with handles clear. Keep figurine shelves and the west-wall doorway unobstructed. Allowance includes these covers; do not frost the doors permanently.
rooms.title: Media room

rooms.recommendation: Washable light-filtering privacy roller shades; no loose drapes
rooms.coverage: Large two-sash exterior window and smaller portico-side window; no curtains on the internal doors.
rooms.why: Shades control mirror glare and street privacy without loose fabric in future equipment space. Workout use does not require blackout.
rooms.day: Raise or partly lower shades to reduce mirror glare.
rooms.night: Lower privacy shades for exercise with the lights on.
rooms.installation: Choose cordless, wipeable material; keep northwest closet access, mirror and quote clear. Room remains unfurnished and equipment-free in this design.
rooms.title: Studio gym

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment
rooms.coverage: Bath #3 is windowless in the documented layout.
rooms.why: There is no exterior glazing to dress. Do not add a curtain allowance for a reflected or imagined opening.
rooms.day: Use planned task and ambient lighting.
rooms.night: Privacy comes from the bathroom door.
rooms.installation: Verify the existing room during survey; revise only if an actual exterior opening is found.
rooms.title: Bath #3

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + hidden privacy shades; no mandatory blackout
rooms.coverage: Terrace-facing glazing. Leave the two high horizontal transoms beside the fireplace bare unless glare or a neighboring sightline requires treatment.
rooms.why: This is a social room with a TV, so flexible glare control and evening privacy matter more than cinema-level darkness. The airy main-floor appearance stays intact.
rooms.day: Sheers diffuse sun; adjust the privacy shade where glare reaches the TV.
rooms.night: Close privacy shades when the room is visible from outside.
rooms.installation: Coordinate a traversing solution at operable terrace glass; stacks must clear handles and passage. Quote a blackout-fabric upgrade separately only if daytime TV testing shows it is wanted. High-transom treatment is not assumed in the base allowance.
rooms.title: Great room

rooms.recommendation: Wipeable privacy roller at the counter window
rooms.coverage: Kitchen counter window only. Adjacent sunroom window banks are counted in the sunroom.
rooms.why: The kitchen needs daylight and evening privacy, with a finish that tolerates cooking and cleaning. Full-length drapes are impractical at a counter or splash area.
rooms.day: Raise or partly lower for working light and glare control.
rooms.night: Lower the non-see-through privacy shade.
rooms.installation: Select washable material and a compact cordless mechanism; survey faucet, backsplash, handles and appliance clearances. No blackout required.
rooms.title: Kitchen

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + discreet privacy shades at tall windows
rooms.coverage: Four tall dining openings: two rectangular windows with shallow transoms on the east facade and two arched windows on the south facade. The smaller high-sill arch near the open living junction stays bare unless a sightline check requires coverage. Preserve the real butler-pantry passage; the oblique photo feature is not a proven closed niche.
rooms.why: Dinner after dark requires privacy while daytime entertaining benefits from light. Heavy blackout is unnecessary and should not obscure the arched architecture when open.
rooms.day: Sheers filter daylight; privacy layers fully raised and curtain stacks off glass.
rooms.night: Lower the privacy layer at all tall openings.
rooms.installation: Survey each opening individually. Mount the privacy layer to cover the whole tall opening, including an arch when closed, while clearing its shape when raised. Verify space above arches; price any required specialty arch treatment separately instead of assuming a standard roller fits.
rooms.title: Formal dining

rooms.recommendation: Clear ivory sheers + hidden privacy/glare shades
rooms.coverage: TWO real tall living windows along EAST facade (printed-plan BOTTOM). NORTH facade decorative False Window stays solid inside. Keep the south dining seam and west hall connection open.
rooms.why: Maintain the bright piano salon and soft Cloud-style seating, with privacy after dark. An adjustable layer also helps reduce direct sun at the piano; sheers alone are not a complete sun-protection strategy.
rooms.day: Sheers drawn lightly; shade only where direct sun or glare calls for it.
rooms.night: Lower privacy shades on the front windows.
rooms.installation: Coordinate stack-back with piano lid, seating and circulation; confirm piano placement and environmental guidance with the chosen manufacturer. No blackout requirement.
rooms.title: Living room · piano salon

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + independent privacy shades by window bank
rooms.coverage: Wraparound lower glazing and terrace-door glass as measured. High transoms stay open visually unless an actual sightline or glare issue requires coverage.
rooms.why: The six-seat breakfast area should feel bright. Separate shades let you manage individual sunny sides and evening privacy without making the whole room dark.
rooms.day: Use sheers; lower only the shade on the sunniest side as needed.
rooms.night: Close the privacy layer where neighbors can see in.
rooms.installation: Split shade zones at real mullions and provide a compatible operable-door solution. Keep fabric and stacks clear of oven/cooking surfaces and door travel. Match the main-floor sheer color; no heavy blackout lining in the base.
rooms.title: Sunroom

rooms.recommendation: Bare high glazing by default; privacy review before ordering
rooms.coverage: Existing high stacked stair windows.
rooms.why: The landing and quarter-turn stair benefit from daylight; loose drapes would add clutter at circulation. No sleep or cinema use requires blackout.
rooms.day: Keep glass open visually; add fixed diffusion only if glare warrants it.
rooms.night: Check views from neighboring upper floors; height alone does not guarantee privacy.
rooms.installation: No new covering in the base budget. If the survey reveals a sightline, price a discreet privacy treatment and safe operating/cleaning access separately. Keep fabric away from treads and guards.
rooms.title: Second-floor stair hall

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + fully closing oatmeal blackout-lined curtains
rooms.coverage: All FOUR real west sash units. Coordinate every real retreat opening as part of the same open sleep-darkening zone; interior vestibule transom is not an exterior window.
rooms.why: Sleeping darkness and evening privacy require covering the full bedroom/retreat exterior inventory because the connection is open.
rooms.day: Sheers filter daylight; opaque layer stacks clear of all windows and dresser.
rooms.night: Fully close bedroom and retreat exterior blackout layers; use gentle bed/bedside light for winding down and switch off for sleep as preferred.
rooms.installation: Independent tracks with overlap/returns. Resolve west-window dresser, curtain drop and stack with measured elevations; concealed blackout rollers behind sheers can avoid trapped fabric. Do not curtain the interior retreat connection or add unselected dresser lighting.
rooms.title: Owners suite

rooms.recommendation: Match owners bedroom: ivory sheers + fully closing blackout layers
rooms.coverage: THREE real west sash units and TWO photographed south side units. Any north optional terrace-door glazing remains conditional on actual-house confirmation; no door is added to the open bedroom connection.
rooms.why: Retreat exterior light enters the open owners bedroom, so every real opening belongs to one sleep-darkening zone.
rooms.day: Sheers soften light for reading and coffee; blackout layers stack clear.
rooms.night: Fully close all real retreat window blackout layers together with the four-unit owners-bedroom bank.
rooms.installation: Measure the full west bank including the third unit cropped in model photos. Keep fabric clear of bar, appliances and actual door operations. Optional door/exterior-spiral features are not new confirmed window counts or new allowance items.
rooms.title: Owners retreat

rooms.recommendation: Moisture-resistant opaque privacy shade at the ONE real dry window
rooms.coverage: ONE south dry exterior opening near tub/vanity only. Apparent left/shower-side window is reflection on/in enclosure glass, not a second exterior opening.
rooms.why: Bathing privacy requires a fully closing shade at the real window. Reflected glazing receives no separate treatment; bedroom blackout can be managed with the bathroom door closed.
rooms.day: Adjust or raise the dry-window shade for diffuse daylight; glass reflections show that same shape and shade position.
rooms.night: Fully close the real dry-window opaque privacy shade; the shower-glass reflection must also show closed coverage with no open blue window.
rooms.installation: Measure and select one moisture-resistant opaque shade with fixing and edge coverage suitable for the dry opening. Remove the unsupported separate shower-window film/glazing claim. Preserve existing numeric allowance until a measured revised quote; no fabric in spray and no new shower opening.
rooms.title: Owners bathroom

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment
rooms.coverage: Windowless closet in the current plan-led concept.
rooms.why: No exterior opening needs a covering; preserve storage and task lighting.
rooms.day: Use closet lighting.
rooms.night: Privacy is provided by the suite and closet enclosure.
rooms.installation: Confirm during measured survey; do not invent a window to match a render reflection.
rooms.title: Owners walk-in closet

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout-lined curtains or concealed blackout roller
rooms.coverage: Plan-BOTTOM wider paired front bank and plan-RIGHT narrow side opening. Headboard remains TOP stair-hall wall; closet at LOWER plan-LEFT shared-bath boundary away from TOP-LEFT hall entry.
rooms.why: A sleeping room needs darkness and nighttime privacy even when also used for study. The desk is not a reason to omit blackout.
rooms.day: Sheers and an adjustable shade position for study light.
rooms.night: Fully close blackout at both real opening groups; preserve their original positions and window operation.
rooms.installation: Measure tracks/rollers after fixing the lower closet and hall-entry relationship. Keep the side-window desk clear of shade operation; use suitable blackout overlap behind sheers where curtains cannot stack. No second closet or relocated exterior window.
rooms.title: Bedroom 2

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout at every exterior opening
rooms.coverage: Three exterior opening groups: paired front bank on plan-BOTTOM/east, plus TWO separate windows flanking headboard on plan-LEFT/south.
rooms.why: All three openings must darken for comfortable sleeping; dressing only the large window would leave the bedside windows admitting light.
rooms.day: Sheers preserve a light guest-bedroom atmosphere.
rooms.night: Close blackout at all three opening groups; maintain the same bed/window-wall orientation in adjacent bathroom glimpses.
rooms.installation: Use functional lined curtains where stack space allows and matching discreet blackout rollers behind sheers at tight bedside openings. Check bedside furniture, wall lights and bedding clearance before fixing tracks.
rooms.title: Bedroom 3

rooms.recommendation: No covering in photographed vanity zone; wet-compartment opening pending confirmation
rooms.coverage: No exterior opening is visible in current vanity-zone views. Bedroom glazing through doors/mirrors belongs to those bedrooms. The small front/toilet-side opening in the separate wet compartment is UNCONFIRMED as interior glazing.
rooms.why: Avoid ordering a treatment for a bedroom reflection or falsely certifying the full shared bath as windowless. Bathing privacy in the unvisualized wet compartment depends on its actual opening inventory.
rooms.day: Use vanity lighting; bedroom sheers belong to the adjoining rooms. Verify wet-compartment glazing before a treatment decision.
rooms.night: Close bathroom internal doors as appropriate and adjoining bedroom blackout layers. Any confirmed wet-compartment glazing would need its own measured privacy solution.
rooms.installation: Keep current zero allowance and system classification unchanged pending homeowner/as-built confirmation. If the specific wet-compartment opening is real, add a separately quoted moisture-compatible privacy treatment; do not create a window in current vanity crops.
rooms.title: Shared bathroom

rooms.recommendation: Washable privacy rollers; lined woven-look shades as an alternative
rooms.coverage: Two separately cased sink/counter-side openings: near arched-top window and farther rectangular window.
rooms.why: Laundry needs useful daylight, washable finishes and evening privacy. Open-weave decorative shades alone may be see-through; blackout and floor-length curtains are unnecessary.
rooms.day: Raise for task light; adjust to soften glare.
rooms.night: Fully close opaque privacy coverage across ALL glass in both openings, including the near arched head and both sills/side edges. A rectangular shade beneath an uncovered arch is incomplete.
rooms.installation: Measure the full arched opening, separately cased rectangular opening and sink/faucet clearance. Provide a custom opaque arched-head infill or suitable full-opening system paired with the operable lower shade; cover ALL glass at night. Keep fabrics clear of wet surfaces. Preserve exact “Rinse and repeat..” lettering and current numeric allowances until measured quotes.
rooms.title: Laundry

rooms.recommendation: Bare high windows; add privacy only if sightlines require it
rooms.coverage: THREE separate high 2×2 upper stair-hall windows.
rooms.why: Daylight supports circulation; the stair does not need blackout or floor-length fabric.
rooms.day: Leave glass visually open; assess glare on the landing.
rooms.night: High glazing stays bare in the current night study; verify actual neighboring sightlines before any later privacy change.
rooms.installation: No covering in current allowance. Preserve daylight, guards and stair travel; no floor-length fabric, new windows or stair runner. Any later discreet privacy treatment requires a separate measured quote.
rooms.title: Third-floor stair hall

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + independent privacy layers at terrace glazing
rooms.coverage: South French-door glazing, ONE small flank window each side, wide west terrace slider and compact southwest bar window.
rooms.why: The penthouse lounge should retain its views by day and privacy after dark. Being on the top floor does not guarantee privacy from adjacent homes. It is not currently a sleeping room or dedicated cinema.
rooms.day: Sheers for soft light; raise the compact bar-window shade.
rooms.night: Fully close opaque privacy layers at all lower real exterior glazing, especially BOTH small flank windows down to their sills with no exposed dark strips.
rooms.installation: Keep traversing stacks clear of French doors and slider. Compact fitted shades cover each flank and bar window fully; maintain handles and door operation. Sleeping-room blackout is not required for this lounge unless its use changes; current allowances stay unchanged.
rooms.title: Penthouse lounge

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout at the two planned guest-bedroom windows
rooms.coverage: TWO separated east openings in proposed new Bedroom5, opposite the west headboard. The room is unbuilt and final real opening inventory needs measured new-room drawings.
rooms.why: The proposed room will be used for sleeping; integrate privacy and darkness with its enclosure and future storage without changing the window wall.
rooms.day: Ivory sheers filter light; opaque layers open clear of the two planned openings.
rooms.night: Fully close blackout at both confirmed sleeping-room windows, with the exact same bed/door/closet geometry as day.
rooms.installation: Provisional existing allowance retained. Coordinate tracks, returns, support and operation with the west headboard, south closet and north entry/linen route. Do not add a third center interior window from external dormer appearance or drape solid walls.
rooms.title: Penthouse guest bedroom

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment in the current layout
rooms.coverage: No exterior opening shown in the plan-led Bath4; west vestibule entry, north vanity/toilet and east shower remain.
rooms.why: No exterior glazing needs dressing in the documented concept.
rooms.day: Use bathroom lighting.
rooms.night: Use the bathroom door for privacy.
rooms.installation: Verify the actual enclosure and services before final scope. Current zero treatment allowance stays unchanged; any newly discovered real opening requires a separately quoted wet-area privacy specification.
rooms.title: Penthouse bathroom

rooms.recommendation: No interior drapes outdoors
rooms.coverage: Outdoor roof terrace; adjacent interior glazing is covered under loft or suite schedules. Optional outside spiral remains unconfirmed at actual house.
rooms.why: Interior sheers and blackout panels do not belong in this outdoor exposure. Existing exterior shade structures and weather-rated furniture form a separate scope.
rooms.day: Use the existing outdoor shade arrangement.
rooms.night: Close the relevant interior privacy layers from inside.
rooms.installation: No exterior curtains or duplicated interior glazing cost. Current treatment allowance remains unchanged; confirming optional stair does not authorize a new roof or terrace extension.
rooms.title: Roof terrace
